patch.value: The Windows nightly leg cannot separate product defects from harness noise: 744 hardcoded POSIX path literals and 203 raw errno strings in the suite fail on Windows for reasons unrelated to pm behaviour

GH-791 (windows-latest / Node 24, commit d885d5a0) fails four tests. Exactly one of them is a product defect - the merge-safety workspace_root canonicalization tracked as pm-ihmfs6, which also fails on macOS. The other three are properties of the suite, not of pm:

1. tests/unit/sdk/merge-safety.spec.ts 'installs idempotent git attributes/config and exercises the CLI adapter' - same path-spelling family as pm-ihmfs6.
2. tests/unit/packages/guide-shell-runtime.spec.ts 'builds completion registries and list helpers across schema shapes' - asserts listAllItemMetadata was called with the literal '/tmp/pm' (lines 24, 28, 120, 136, 142). On Windows path.resolve('/tmp/pm') is C:\tmp\pm, so the assertion cannot hold and never could.
3. tests/unit/sdk/context-integrity-primitives.spec.ts 'invalidates derived drift state after conventional history writes' - asserts the warning string history_drift_cache_invalidation_failed:ENOTDIR. Windows raises a different errno for the same condition. This one has a product tail worth deciding separately: the diagnostic code embeds a raw platform errno, so the warning an agent parses is platform-dependent.

Census of the class across tests/: 744 hardcoded POSIX absolute path literals matching "/(tmp|home|var|usr)/ in 81 files (worst: extension-loader.spec.ts 159, search-command.spec.ts 137, extensions-runtime.spec.ts 48, builtin-extension-entrypoints.spec.ts 39, telemetry-runtime.spec.ts 34, settings-store.spec.ts 30), plus 203 raw errno literals.

Why this matters more than tidiness: the Windows leg has been red often enough (pm-e70zh5 records a 32/84 scheduled-run failure rate) that a red leg carries no information. Today it is red for one real cross-platform defect and three artifacts, and nothing in the failure output distinguishes them - somebody has to read four stack traces to learn that. The suite is asserting on the harness's temp-directory conventions rather than on pm, so a genuine Windows regression would arrive already camouflaged.

Remedy: route path literals through the existing helpers (withTempPmPath, mockPosixPath) or path.join from os.tmpdir(), and assert on normalized error classes rather than raw errno strings. Prefer a lint rule or a gate over a one-time sweep, since the count grows with every new spec.
No test asserts on a hardcoded POSIX absolute path or a raw platform errno string; a red Windows nightly leg names only product defects

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Cross-platform nightly is GREEN on main again, verified by dispatch 2026-07-28. Run 30372071932 on main succeeded in 7m31s with every leg passing, immediately after PR#795 merged at 14:20:36Z.

The preceding red streak was pre-fix, not an unowned regression: the last three scheduled runs on main failed (30334992958 at 06:29Z today, 30246735868 on 07-27, 30191427127 on 07-26), all on the same two legs, macos-latest Node 24 and windows-latest Node 24, and the actual failures were four specs — guide-shell-runtime building completion registries across schema shapes, context-integrity-primitives invalidating derived drift state after conventional history writes, and merge-safety twice for installing idempotent git attributes and for preferring explicit tracker paths over protected source coordinates. Every scheduled run predated the merge, and PR#795's own branch was named for this work and had already been verified by dispatch, run 30361026722 passing at 12:54Z.

The durable lesson for this item rather than the incident: a scheduled-only signal necessarily reports a stale verdict for as long as the interval, so a red nightly on main is not evidence of a live defect until the last completed run postdates the last merge. Confirm by dispatch before filing anything, and compare the run start against the merge timestamp rather than against the calendar day.
